## Benchmark/task selection

Tests were selected as hard (75-100th percentile) and medium (75th-50th precentile) with the second criteria being maximum token usage to make potential differences more visible.

- TODO: Define the benchmark and task-selection process.

## Models and agent harnesses

### Model Selection
The goal when selecting our models is to cover as many model families as possible, to see if a harness is better overall.

Confirmed models: Kimi K3 Max, GLM 5.3 Flash
Upcoming models to test: Opus 5 medium
Depends on the budget: GPT 5.6 LUNA vs GPT 5.6 Sol high.

### Harness selection
We have chose to Test OpenAI Codex and Claude code, the first party agent harnesses from the frontier ai labs.
Opencode is the second most popular ai harness in the company, and Pi is very known in the community for being efficient.

To make sure the results stay relevant over a longer time, we elected to test opencode V2, the upcoming major rewrite of opencode.

## Experimental setup

- TODO: Describe the experimental setup and controlled variables.

We are sticking to the upstream provider setup.
if a harness has specific upstream provider optimizations, such as remote compaction in codex or tool call behavior in claude code, these are left turned on, we are testing how harnesses behave across models in a real world scenario.

### Setup decisions.
- GPT models have increased pricing past 272k context window, codex cli ignores the full 1m context window and will use 272k unless overriden.
We've decided to use the same limited context window 272k window in other harnesses for the sake of comparison and not let the price difference due to the used context affect the results, and it's only a config option compared to remote compaction.

- Remote compaction. GPT models use a remote compaction endpoint for compacting chat history.
We are only running stock harnesses here, pi can support remote compaction through plugins, but plugins are out of scope.
Opencode V2 has native remote compaction support.

### Compatibility interventions and controlled patches

The benchmark compares agent harness behavior rather than failures caused by
protocol incompatibilities between a harness and the shared model endpoint.
Compatibility interventions were therefore permitted when they were required to
make a harness use the intended model and provider path. These interventions
were kept as small as possible, pinned to exact revisions or container-image
digests, and verified with dedicated acceptance tests. They were not used to add
new harness capabilities or to change the benchmark prompt or tool set.

#### CLIProxyAPI backport between Codex runs

Codex 0.151.0 uses the OpenAI Responses protocol, while the third-party models
in this benchmark are routed through LiteLLM to Fireworks using Chat
Completions. CLIProxyAPI v7.2.146 was therefore used as a protocol bridge for
the Codex runs.

During the benchmark period, an upstream CLIProxyAPI defect was identified in
this translation path [@cliproxyIssue5659]. If one streamed Chat Completions
delta contained both non-empty `reasoning_content` and non-empty `content`, the
translator processed the visible content first and then opened a new reasoning
item. This produced an invalid Responses item order. In the upstream
reproduction, Codex displayed a truncated assistant message even though the
complete generated message was retained in the Codex session file.

The completed Kimi K3 run had already used the unmodified v7.2.146 bridge. Its
CLIProxyAPI request logs were therefore checked retrospectively for the exact
trigger condition. No streamed delta containing both non-empty `content` and
`reasoning_content` was found, so the defect's triggering condition was absent
from that run.

For subsequent third-party Codex runs, the bridge was not upgraded to a newer
CLIProxyAPI release because that would also have introduced unrelated protocol
translation changes. Instead, the benchmark uses a fork based on the exact
v7.2.146 source revision with only the upstream fix for this defect backported
[@cliproxyFix5659]. The fix changes the processing order so that reasoning is
handled before visible content when both occur in the same upstream chunk. For
chunks containing only reasoning, only content, or reasoning followed by a tool
call, the relevant translation behavior is unchanged.

This creates one documented infrastructure difference between the completed
Kimi K3 run and later third-party Codex runs. The change was chosen because it
removes a known malformed Responses sequence while minimizing the experimental
delta. The demonstrated upstream failure was a streaming/client-display defect,
not loss of generated model text; however, malformed Responses item ordering
could in principle affect client state during an agentic tool loop. Applying the
narrow backport avoids that uncertainty without adopting unrelated proxy
changes. The fork revision, image digest, regression test, and acceptance tests
are recorded in `benchmark/bridges/codex-cliproxy/BACKPORT-5659.md`.

#### Codex
For non-native models, Codex's minimal unknown-model fallback metadata was replaced by a standardized metadata profile derived from GPT-5.6 Sol in the pinned Codex version. This prevents model-recognition status from changing the Codex harness capability set. Model-specific capabilities were adjusted to the respective model, while backend-dependent features that could not be supported uniformly were disabled.

Disabled features for non-gpt models: multi_agents v2 and responses lite. 
GPT use the built in model configuration shipped in the forzen release.


#### Opencode V2

At the time of testing. opencode v2 is still in beta, with some bugs particularly effecting setting the maximum output tokens for the upstream provider.
Our upstream provider for Kimi k3, Deepseek v4/v4.1 flash and GLM 5.3 flash is Fireworks ai. and the default for unset values is [2k maximum completion tokens](https://docs.fireworks.ai/faq/models/inference/limitations-controls).
Due to this issue we had to modify the config file to explicitly define the max completion token amount in the body config to workaround the bug [#47398](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47398)
